statement: For $i = \sqrt{-1}$, which of the following is equal to $(4 - 3i) - (-2 + 5i)$?

choices.misconception: I subtracted the $-2$ correctly but did not distribute the minus sign to the $5i$, so I added it to $-3i$.
I added the two complex numbers instead of subtracting the second one from the first.
I subtracted the $5i$ correctly but did not distribute the minus sign to the $-2$, so I added it to 4.

hints: Subtracting a complex number means subtracting both its real part and its imaginary part.
Now combine $4 - 3i + 2 - 5i$, real parts with real parts and imaginary parts with imaginary parts.

solutions.reliable: Distribute the minus sign: $(4 - 3i) - (-2 + 5i) = 4 - 3i + 2 - 5i$. The real parts give $4 + 2 = 6$ and the imaginary parts give $-3i - 5i = -8i$, so the result is $6 - 8i$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
